## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Paṭhamasūcivimānavatthu* ("Needle Mansion", Vv 58) is a canonical verse text belonging to the *Vimānavatthu* collection in the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya. In this discourse, a deva describes their celestial mansion and explains how the karmic fruit of generosity is always greater than the offering made.

 According to automated analysis by DharmaNexus, the text exhibits substantial Pali-internal text reuse, sharing 109 passages across 15 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Unsurprisingly, the most extensive overlap occurs with the commentary, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (50 matches covering §1.1–4.3) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, substantial formulaic verses describing celestial splendor and stock poetic lines are shared with numerous other *Vimānavatthu* discourses, notably *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Ambavimānavatthu* (Vv 79), *Phaladāyakavimānavatthu* (Vv 67), *Paṭhamakaraṇīyavimānavatthu* (Vv 56), and its direct counterpart *Dutiyasūcivimānavatthu* (Vv 59) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matching, DharmaNexus detects low-similarity alignments with the alternative Chinese translation of the *Saṃyuktāgama* (*Bieyi za ahan jing*, T 100) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
